name: Uruguay
headline_status: Uruguay was the first country to fully legalise recreational cannabis; registered adult citizens and residents can grow it, join clubs or buy it in pharmacies.
summary: Law 19.172, promulgated on 20 December 2013, created a state-regulated cannabis market overseen by the IRCCA. Registered adults 18+ can choose one of three routes: growing up to six plants at home, joining a cannabis club, or buying up to 40 g a month in licensed pharmacies, which began selling in 2017. Visitors are currently excluded, but in early 2026 the regulator said it was studying ways to let non-residents buy legally.

adult_use_since.value: Law 19.172 was promulgated on 20 December 2013 and published on 7 January 2014; pharmacy sales began in 2017.

possession_limit.value: Up to 40 g of marijuana is presumed to be for personal use, plus the harvest of up to six home-grown plants kept at home or a club member's share. Registered pharmacy buyers may purchase up to 10 g a week and 40 g a month.

home_grow.value: Up to six flowering plants per household, with a harvest of no more than 480 g a year; growers must be adult Uruguayan citizens or permanent residents registered with the IRCCA.

purchase_age.value: 18. People under 18 may not access psychoactive cannabis for recreational use.

retail_sales.value: Sold in IRCCA-licensed pharmacies to registered buyers, up to 10 g a week and 40 g a month. Membership clubs of 15 to 45 members may grow up to 99 plants.

regulator.value: Institute for the Regulation and Control of Cannabis (IRCCA), created by Law 19.172.

tourists.value: Non-residents cannot buy legally: pharmacy buyers, home growers and club members must be Uruguayan citizens or permanent residents registered with the IRCCA. In 2026 the IRCCA said it was studying allowing tourists, students and temporary workers to buy under controlled conditions.

timeline.event: President Mujica promulgates Law 19.172 legalising and regulating cannabis
Pharmacy sales to registered users begin
IRCCA says it is evaluating legal sales to non-resident foreigners

pending.item: Regulatory change to let non-resident foreigners, including tourists, buy legal cannabis.
pending.status: Under evaluation by the IRCCA since early 2026; nothing approved.

faq.a: Yes. Registered adults can grow up to six plants, join a cannabis club or buy up to 40 g a month at licensed pharmacies.

faq.q: Can tourists buy weed in Uruguay?
faq.a: Not currently. Only registered citizens and residents can buy, though the regulator is studying opening sales to visitors.

faq.q: How much weed can you buy in Uruguay?
faq.a: Registered pharmacy customers can buy up to 40 g per month.
